title: Meet the seed twin
subtitle: One Arabidopsis seed, from dry seed to seedling
description: A tour of what the model simulates: water uptake, the hormones that hold and release dormancy, the wave of cell expansion that ends in germination, oxygen inside the seed, and the seedling that follows. Read this first; every other story uses the same views.

scenes.title: Meet the seed twin
lines: A 3D model of one Arabidopsis seed, from the moment it takes up water to a five-day-old seedling.
Every cell is simulated: water, oxygen, hormones and growth. The geometry is schematic, built from published anatomy rather than a microscope scan.

captions.text: The seed is cut away so you can see inside: seed coat (brown), endosperm (pale), and the embryo coloured by tissue.
Water floods in. By {A.t@12|0} h the seed holds {A.water_gg@12|2} g of water per gram of dry seed, and its mucilage coat swells.
Left: abscisic acid, which holds the seed dormant. Right: gibberellin, which drives germination.
Once wet, the embryo breaks ABA down: by {A.t@12|0} h it has fallen from {A.aba_mean@0|2} to {A.aba_mean@12|2}, while gibberellin builds up from the radicle tip.
Cells begin to expand in the lower hypocotyl and the expansion spreads along the axis: the pattern Bassel and colleagues measured cell by cell in 3D.
The seed coat splits at {A.testa_rupture_h|1} h, and the radicle pushes through the endosperm at {A.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h. That is germination.
Respiring tissue uses oxygen faster than it can diffuse in. At {A.t@34|0} h the seed surface sits at {A.o2_surface_kpa@34|1} kPa but the core of the axis falls to {A.o2_core_min_kpa@34|2} kPa.
Root hairs anchor the seedling at {A.anchored_h|1} h; the root turns down with gravity and the hypocotyl lifts the cotyledons out.
The cotyledons leave the seed coat at {A.cot_emerged_h|1} h and, in the light, open at {A.cot_open_h|1} h.
By {A.t@120|0} h the root is {A.root_len_um@120/1000|1} mm long and the hypocotyl {A.hyp_len_um@120/1000|1} mm.
